podcast.title: Academy of Country Music Award
podcast.body: In 1973, 20 years after his career began, he received a "most promising new come of award" from the Academy of Country Music, marking his successful transition into country music. "He eventually received a most promising new come of award from the Academy of Country Music in 1973, 20 years after his career started."

podcast.title: Childhood Guitar Incident
podcast.body: When Dorsey was eight, his mother bought him a guitar, which, by the end of the day, he had broken over Johnny's head in a fight. "By the end of the day both guitars had been broken over each other's heads."

podcast.title: Early Group with Elvis Presley
podcast.body: Dorsey grew up around Lauderdale Court, the same apartment block as Elvis Presley, and used to sing with a gang of teenage boys. "They'd grown up around Loddardale Court, the same apartment block where Elbas Presley spent his teenage years and they used to hang around together and sing with the gang of teenage boys that included Bill Blacks for the Johnny."

podcast.body: Dorsey was a trained boxer and became the Golden Gloves champion of the South in 1950, even having once fought Sonny Liston. podcast.title: Quitting Rock and Roll Trio Before Film
podcast.body: Dorsey was the first to quit the Rock and Roll Trio, leaving a few days before they were due to appear in the film "Rock, Rock, Rock," although he later rejoined. "Lucy was the first to quit."

podcast.title: Sibling Rivalry with Johnny
podcast.body: Dorsey and his brother Johnny were notorious for fighting violently and often, making their relationship one of constant conflict within their musical partnership. "But few pairs of brothers have fought as violently and as often as Johnny and Dorsey Bennett."

podcast.title: Songwriting Credit Splitting for "Tear It Up"
podcast.body: When Dorsey quickly wrote the song "Tear It Up," he decided to split the credit four ways: among the three band members and their manager, a common practice for bands operating as a cohesive unit at the time. "While Dorsey wrote that song, he decided to split the credit as they always did, four ways, between the three members of the band and their manager."
